title: Opex 11/06
subtitle: Seven stocks, zero buys (yet). Every name waits for its trigger.
read: Friday was ugly: S&P -1.8%, Nasdaq -2.9%, and Intel's guidance took about $1 trillion out of chip stocks in a day.
The Fed held on 10/28, but two of the twelve voted to hike. Next meeting Dec 8-9.
Nothing here is a buy at Friday's close. Long shares or calls only; sizes in R (1R = what you'll lose on one trade).
dates: Monthly opex, NFLX and PYPL deadline
ADI earnings, the real TXN risk

stocks.name: PayPal
stocks.trigger: Dip to $55.00-55.50 that closes in the upper half of the day
stocks.deadline: No dip by Fri 11/20, no trade. No breakout entry.
why: About 10x earnings, ~$9.4B left on the buyback
Low beta (0.58), barely moves with the rest
watch: New CEO since February, branded checkout not growing
August's $62.58 was a buyout bid that died ($60.50, 8/28)

stocks.name: Texas Instruments
stocks.trigger: A: dip to $288-292 (stop $283)   B: close over $310 (stop $300)
why: ~16% over its 200-day, no November earnings
Friday's -3.9% was ex-dividend day; real drop ~3.4% vs SOXX -8.2%
IV rank 30, IV 1.15x realized: fairly priced
watch: ADI moves with it (0.90) and reports Tue 11/24
$7.5B Silicon Labs deal, China review open

stocks.name: EQT
why: Only negative beta on the list (-0.27): when chips puke, gas mostly shrugs
Back above the 200-day, dealer support at $55
Reported 10/27, no earnings this month
watch: All-stock Range Resources deal: arb hedging slows the upside

stocks.name: NVIDIA

Four straight beats, guide assumes zero China

stocks.name: Amazon

AWS +39%, fastest in about five years
